[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] TierPoint is headquartered at 12444 Powerscourt Drive, Suite 450, in St. Louis, Missouri, and traces to 2010, when the company acquired its first data center in Dallas, Texas. Argo Infrastructure Partners increased its ownership stake and capital commitment to TierPoint in a transaction reported in December 2025, following an earlier round in which TierPoint closed $320 million in equity from a consortium of investors.

The companys own site describes a portfolio of 40 data center facilities across 20 US markets coast-to-coast, serving thousands of companies spanning small businesses to Fortune 500 enterprises across both public and private sectors.

The registry here tracks 3 TierPoint facilities across three states, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Texas, a small subset of the companys 20 named markets. TierPoints origin in a 2010 Dallas acquisition and its continued Texas presence in this registry connect it to the same Dallas-Fort Worth corridor already carrying Stream, Digital Realty, and Aligned facilities recorded elsewhere in this registry. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as TierPoint in Tulsa, OK, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to TierPoint based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
TierPoint in Tulsa, Oklahoma, is operated by , but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

TierPoint holds 6 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), ITAR (a specific compliance or security standard), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Oklahoma has 1 facility mapped in this site's dataset, of which 0 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 0 MW.
